ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized agents against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian sanctions lists administered under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, the Canadian Criminal Code terrorist entity lists, and PEP databases (politically exposed persons including domestic and foreign PEPs). Enhanced due diligence applies when any UBO is a PEP, when ownership is opaque/nominee-based, or when funds originate from high-risk or FATF-monitored jurisdictions. For this low-risk bonded trucking/TIR sector, standard KYC, source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring are required given fuel-card clearing and SWIFT wire rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES), administered by Service Alberta and filed through authorized Registry Agents; official reference portal: https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must be composed of English/French alphabetic characters, Arabic numerals, or recognized punctuation; names in non-Latin scripts must be accompanied by a certified transliteration into English or French. The name must be distinct from existing Alberta corporations, extra-provincial registrations, and federal names appearing in the NUANS database, and must not be confusingly similar or contrary to public policy.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Insurance, Assurance, Loan, and any term implying financial services regulated under the Bank Act or the Alberta Insurance Act
Royal, Crown, Government, Federal, Provincial, Municipal, and any term connoting official governmental authority
University, College, Institute, and any educational designation requiring ministerial consent
Engineer, Engineering, Architect, Lawyer, Doctor, Medical, and any regulated professional designation restricted by Alberta statutory practice statutes
Canada, Alberta, Calgary, Edmonton, and any geographic indicator implying sponsorship, endorsement, or governmental affiliation
TIR, Customs, Border, Bonded, and similar trade-infrastructure tokens that may mislead as to federal/customs licensing unless the applicant demonstrates qualification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects or conditions a name, the applicant or an authorized Alberta Registry Agent must submit a written reconsideration request to the Director, Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, within 30 days of rejection, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, prior-use documentation, or letters of consent from the adversely affected name-holder. No further extension of a NUANS report is granted after the 90-day validity window; a new NUANS search is required. If the Director upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review or proceed with an alternate name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office address may be virtual and maintained by a licensed commercial registered-agent service in Alberta, as required by the Alberta Business Corporations Act. However, for ISIC 5221 long-haul bonded highway trucking under TIR Carnets, a virtual address is not sufficient for operational substance; the carrier must maintain a physical Alberta operating terminal/principal place of business where vehicle records, drivers' logs, customs documents, and TIR Carnet custody records can be produced for Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and Alberta Transportation audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% -- moderate annual risk of unannounced on-site inspection by Alberta Transportation, CBSA bonded-carrier auditors, or fuel-tax enforcement officers because cross-border bonded trucking involves customs seals, excise-fuel accounting, and regulated commercial-vehicle safety.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9 (ABCA) - ss. 8-10 (incorporation), s. 101 (registered office), Part 8 (directors and officers), s. 24 (certificate correction); Motor Vehicle Transport Act (Canada), RSC 1985, c. 29 (3rd Supp.) for extra-provincial operating authority
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), Corporate Registry Services, 9th Floor, 10155-102 Street NW, Edmonton, Alberta, T5J 4L4; electronic filing via authorized service providers or the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) together with Notice of Registered Office (Form 2) and Notice of Directors (Form 3) filed under the ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a corporation may incorporate with nil issued capital. Shares may be issued for money, property, or past services (ABCA s. 25). No government escrow account is required; any subscription proceeds must be credited to the corporation's own bank account and fully settled before the shares are issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED: (1) the subscription for 10,000 common shares by the sole incorporator is accepted, such shares to be issued upon full payment to the corporate bank account; (2) the registered office of the Corporation within Alberta, as filed with the Corporate Registry, is adopted as the registered records office; (3) the model bylaws are adopted; (4) the following officers are appointed: President/CEO, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer; (5) the corporate seal and banking resolutions are approved, and the officers are authorized to execute statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation via NUANS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) through accredited NUANS search agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an instructed NUANS name search for the proposed corporate name or a numbered name alternative. Provide three ranked name choices and obtain a NUANS search report not older than 90 days. If the name is allowable, file an electronic name reservation request with the Corporate Registry and pay the applicable fee; the reservation remains valid for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or collides with an existing mark, file a new reservation using the next priority name, or seek consent from the conflicting name holder; an appeal may be filed with the Registrar under the ABCA naming rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel; subsequent review by Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) stating the corporate name, share structure (unlimited common shares and noted classes), number and first directors, and any restrictions on business. Attach the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors. Sign the articles by hand or by secure electronic signature; statutory declarations or notarization are not required for domestic filing.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director of each named director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the articles (e.g., naming, director residency, or share class defects), amend the affected clause and resubmit without additional name-reservation fees; deficiencies must be cured within 30 days of the Registry notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Payment at the Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - electronic filing portal or authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Form 1 Articles together with Form 2 and Form 3 through the Alberta Corporate Registry electronic portal or a licensed service provider. Pay the filing fee of CAD 200 plus name reservation fee by credit card or approved debit mechanism. Retain the electronic acknowledgment as proof of submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for technical non-compliance, correct the stated deficiencies and refile; no partial refund is issued, but a fresh certificate will be processed once the resubmitted package is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Organizational Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (certificate); Board of Directors (governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, convene the first board of directors meeting. Adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription and issuance, registered office adoption, bylaw adoption, officer appointments, corporate seal, banking resolutions, and any TIR-related governance mandates. Maintain the minutes in the corporate records book.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting and signed resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For defects in the certificate, apply to the Registrar under ABCA s. 24 for a certificate of correction; governance irregularities are cured by a subsequent unanimous director/shareholder resolution ratifying the prior acts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration and Corporate Records Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA through the Business Registration Online portal to obtain a Business Number (BN) with corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll program accounts. Register the Alberta corporate income tax account; file the corporate registry annual return when due. Prepare the share register, directors' register, and registered office record in the Alberta registered records office.
required_dossiers: CRA RC4022 Business Registration Information form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is delayed or rejected, contact the CRA Business Window with the certificate and a letter of explanation; if the annual return is filed late, apply for reinstatement under the ABCA and pay the late-filing fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Transportation (Motor Transport Services), Registrar of Motor Vehicles, in coordination with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Commercial Programs and Transport Canada
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Carrier Safety Fitness Certificate under the Motor Vehicle Transport Act; CBSA Bonded Carrier Licence; TIR Carnet Holder Authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (EPA) with coordination by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration - trucking depot and storage terminal use falls below the full EIA report threshold under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 276/2003); a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not triggered unless significant new construction or hazardous waste transfer capacity exceeds trigger levels.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with CEPA 1999 for diesel emissions and VOC containment; Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives for nitrogen dioxide and PM2.5; zero discharge of wastewater to groundwater, with all wash-bay water to sanitary sewer under municipal sewer-use bylaws; used oil, antifreeze, and fuel filters managed under the Alberta Recycling Management Authority and hazardous waste regulations; spill containment and emergency response plans under A.R. 214/2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire marshal under the Alberta Fire Code (NFC 2019); building occupancy permit and structural load clearance for the maintenance depot; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHSA) clearance under the OHS Code 2009 for workplace operations; fuel storage and dispensing must pass Alberta Safety Codes Act inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register for statutory TIN/VAT ID via CRA Non-Resident Registration Program on CRA My Account portal or Form NR301; Canadian entities including CA_CORP obtain Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration online portal or Form RC59
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election; hybrid mismatch rules apply under Domestic Matching Rules; specific elections under Income Tax Act sections 85, 86, 87 for corporate reorganizations and amalgamations

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory GST/HST returns filed electronically via CRA My Business Account; real-time digital reporting and clearance for businesses exceeding $30 million annual revenue under GST/HST New Registration Rules

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for 0% GST/HST rate; cross-border trucking services under TIR Carnets qualify if services performed outside Canada or specific export conditions satisfied with proof of export
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (if applicable), Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent proof of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to $100,000 per violation plus interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts with audit adjustments; potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada (central monetary authority and lender of last resort). Exchange-control monitoring and AML/CFT transactional oversight are administered by FINTRAC and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control licensing agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; there are no restrictions on the purchase, sale, or cross-border transfer of CAD or foreign exchange under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52). Profit and dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted but generally triggers Part XIII withholding tax (25% statutory, reduced to 5%-15% under applicable tax treaties, e.g., Canada-US Treaty Article X). Capital repatriation and inbound equity injection are equally unrestricted and do not require regulatory pre-approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio on export proceeds; freight, TIR transit, and cross-border trucking receivables may be retained in USD or any freely convertible currency. For income-tax and GST/HST filing purposes, amounts must be converted to CAD using Bank of Canada daily exchange rates (or a reasonable rate) under Income Tax Act s. 261, but no statutory conversion or repatriation timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Non-bank digital EMIs and payment service providers (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Vialet, Corpay) may be used as supplementary settlement wallets for cross-border vendor payments and fuel-card top-ups, but they cannot hold Canadian demand-deposit bank accounts under the Bank Act and are not eligible as the primary treasury clearing account. Such providers must be registered as money services businesses or PSPs with FINTRAC, and their USD custodial balances are not CDIC-insured; legal risk increases if transaction flows exceed CAD 1M annually without a Schedule I bank anchor account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote onboarding is permitted for an Alberta-incorporated business corporation; no physical appearance of directors at a branch is mandated. KYC requires certified true copies of director/shareholder passports (notarized or consular-apostilled), a corporate records package from the Alberta Corporate Registry (or Corporations Canada), video identity verification, and, where any director holds ≥10% in a foreign-resident entity, enhanced due diligence including source of wealth and a web/teleconference compliance interview. Physical attendance becomes mandatory only if identity verification fails or if the corporate structure involves a FATF high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner resident in or receiving funds from a FATF-listed high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS/FATCA self-certification forms (W-8BEN-E, NR301), apostilled share register and corporate registry extracts, source-of-wealth statements with bank reference letters, signed declaration of beneficial ownership under the Canada Business Corporations Act s. 21.1/21.2, and corroborating TIR Carnet holder licences and freight contracts to evidence legitimate commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cash or cash-equivariant fuel purchases lacking a digital audit trail (fuel-card cash top-offs at truck stops)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Issuer-level fuel card transaction logs (WEX, FleetCor, Comdata, Shell/CorteX), monthly settlement statements, GPS/ELD odometer and geofencing reports, TIR Carnet journey route documentation, CBSA Division 16 arrival/departure manifests, and signed driver expense policies with per-diem limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity USD wire inflows from US freight brokers, factors, or CASS settlement houses that may conceal invoice discounting or factor fraud
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master Transportation Agreements and broker factor agreements, original bills of lading and PODs, ACE/CBP border-crossing records for each TIR movement, invoice-to-wire reconciliation ledgers, and the transport insurance certificates (cargo and liability) naming the bank as additional insured.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity from non-resident shareholders: wire via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire through a US correspondent) with the payment memo 'Share subscription / Paid-in capital - [Shareholder name] - [Company name]'. No exchange-control approval or BOP purpose-code registration is required in Canada; compliance hinges on FINTRAC reporting of any incoming electronic funds transfer ≥ CAD 10,000 and the bank's source-of-funds verification for injections > CAD 100,000. The funds are credited to the Capital Escrow Account at the Schedule I bank and released to the Operating Account upon verification of the corporate share register and articles of amendment (if applicable).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 via bank's correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire) for supplier, driver, customs duty, and US fuel payments; (2) Lynx (Payments Canada's high-value RTGS, formerly LVTS) for same-day CAD settlements; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for capital equipment (tractors/trailers) and bulk fuel procurement from verified counterparties; (4) Cross-border USD ACH (via EFT Canada and US Automated Clearing House) for low-value recurring payments including fuel-card top-ups and toll transponder replenishments; and (5) Commercial card network clearing (Visa, Mastercard, Comdata, CorteX) for fleet fuel and maintenance expenses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts executed with the Schedule I bank dealing room for budgeted fuel, payroll, and inter-company dividend flows
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) for term debt hedging on equipment finance facilities
European-style FX options (CAD/USD and CAD/foreign) for contingent capex bids and seasonally volatile freight-payment flows

FX swap (swap/roll) agreements to roll maturing forward positions without physical settlement; NDFs are excluded from the policy because CAD is fully deliverable and NDF execution would serve no substantive hedging purpose and may breach prudent treasury guidelines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or registration under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); no calendar-year-end alignment and no extension for filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing results in loss of good standing and refusal of certificates of compliance/status; after two consecutive unremedied annual return defaults, the Registrar may publish a Notice of Intention to Strike Off and administratively dissolve the corporation; directors and officers remain personally exposed for post-dissolution liabilities and statutory tax deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director of Corporate Governance, Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Only applicable if CA_CORP is incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act and registered extra-provincially in Alberta; due within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two consecutive missed annual returns may lead to administrative dissolution under s. 212 of the CBCA; revival requires arrears, prescribed fees, and a certificate of revival, and does not automatically relieve directors of pre-dissolution liabilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold triggers a mandatory audit under Alberta law. A mandatory independent audit applies to a distributing corporation and to non-distributing private corporations where the shareholders have not unanimously consented to waive auditor appointment for the financial year, or where a shareholder holding the prescribed voting threshold requests an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable/distributing corporations; private enterprises may choose Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook, or IFRS. Accounting books must be capable of producing financial statements supporting CRA tax returns and T2 reconciliation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta Business Corporations Act documentation requires maintenance of a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC). There is no standalone AB UBO confirmation; prescribed ISC particulars must be reported with the Alberta annual return only where the phased beneficial-ownership filing obligations are in force. A CBCA corporation must report ISC information in the federal annual return. After any share transfer, the ISC register must be updated within 15 days and the annual return must reflect the updated registered office and director information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book containing directors' and shareholders' resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 130–450 per year for a typical Alberta registered office and registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800–7,500 per year for a small/medium private cross-border trucking corporation if a certified audit is required or requested

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined: 15% federal Part I general rate and 8% Alberta general corporate rate (Alberta rate restored to 8%; federal 38% reduced by 10% provincial abatement and 13% general reduction)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday in Canada or Alberta; preferential timing deductions lower effective cash tax: CCA Class 16 (tractors/trailers) 40% declining balance, Class 10 (other rolling equipment) 30%, Class 1 (depot/terminal buildings) 4%; immediate expensing for eligible zero-emission trucks (Class 54/55); small business deduction for CCPCs reduces combined rate to 11% on the first CAD 500,000 active business income; foreign tax credit available for US section 887 gross-basis transportation tax and US state/federal fuel excise taxes

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including embedded Alberta provincial schedules); filed via CRA EFILE T2 XML through approved software or CRA My Business Account; Alberta corporate income tax is collected federally under the tax collection agreement and no separate AB filing portal is used
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly Part I tax instalments are required where the corporation's prior-year basic federal and provincial tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months after year-end (3 months for a qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation with taxable capital of associated group not exceeding CAD 15 million); instalments are due on prescribed quarterly dates

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Alberta corporation number, fiscal period end date, CRA business number (BN) account suffix, and residency status; for a Canadian-resident corporation, enter the full legal entity code and registered office address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident carrier carrying on business in Canada through a PE must use the Canadian BN account and mark the return as a non-resident corporation under ITA s. 150(1)(b); without a Canadian PE, US-resident trucking income is generally treaty-exempt and no T2 is required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total freight haulage revenue, fuel surcharges, detention/demurrage recoveries, customs-bond storage fees, and incidental dispatch commissions; amounts must be converted to Canadian dollars on the elected exchange rate convention
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the Canadian PE in accordance with the permanent establishment profit attribution rules; do not include US-internal trip revenue unless the US revenue is tied to Canadian operations for allocation purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting net income (IFRS or ASPE) to taxable income; add back non-deductible fines, 50% of meals/entertainment, non-deductible vehicle violations, and expenses paid to non-arms-length non-residents lacking documentation; deduct CCA, prior-year non-capital loss carryovers, and treaty-related exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct only expenses reasonably related to earning taxable income sourced to the Canadian PE; intercompany allocations must be supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim CCA on depreciable property used to earn income: Class 16 tractors/trailers 40% DB, Class 10 other automotive assets 30% DB, Class 1 terminal buildings 4% DB, and immediate expensing for eligible zero-emission trucks under Class 54/55; half-year rule applies unless specifically excluded
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CCA is available only for property used by the Canadian PE; assets registered in a foreign country and used exclusively abroad cannot be written off against Canadian taxable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 4 and Alberta Schedule 5 (Provincial allocation and tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate taxable income among provinces using gross revenue and salary/wage factors; Alberta general rate 8% (2% Alberta small business rate) applied to AB-allocated taxable income; federal Part I tax is computed on Schedule 400/401 using the 15% general rate less abatement and SBD
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: US-parented fleets operating from multiple Canadian provinces must file Schedule 4 with the same allocation factors in each province; declare PE locations accurately because CRA cross-checks provincial registrations and insurance filings

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 53 (RDTOH and dividend refund) and Part XIII
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate refundable dividend tax on investment income (RDTOH) and the refund available upon paying taxable dividends; this schedule governs the cash distribution mechanics for an Alberta holding structure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any shareholder is a non-resident, the dividend must be reported on NR4 and Part XIII withholding of 25% (or reduced treaty rate) must be remitted; the refundable dividend refund does not offset the Part XIII obligation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty under ITA s. 162: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of lateness up to 12 months (maximum 17%); repeat-filer penalties are doubled with steeper monthly accruals; arrears interest compounds daily at the CRA prescribed rate; failure to file despite a demand can lead to arbitrary assessment under s. 152(7) and summary conviction fines up to CAD 25,000 under s. 238

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return for Transactions with Non-Arm's-Length Non-Residents; filed electronically through CRA EFILE T2 or My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as the T2 return (6 months after fiscal year-end); T106 is a mandatory information return for the taxation year in which the aggregate gross value of specified transactions with each non-resident non-arm's-length party exceeds CAD 1,000,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List each class of related-party transaction: intercompany dispatch fees, fleet leasing, management and administrative charges, fuel-card settlement fees, insurance pooling, and cost-sharing arrangements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report transactions in the currency of the contract and indicate the exchange rate methodology; a US parent and each Canadian affiliate must be identified by legal name and jurisdiction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Describe the pricing method selected for each transactional class: CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split; provide the rationale for the most reliable method, including comparability factors and functional analysis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State clearly the role of the US parent, Canadian operating corporation, and any intermediate holding entity; the CRA may request comparables for the 5 most recent years and contra-trade retroactive adjustments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Senior financial officer or tax director attestation that the documentation is complete; the signer accepts responsibility for the accuracy of transfer-pricing information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The signer should be resident in Canada where possible; the CRA can impose a gross-negligence penalty personally against the signer for false statements on the T106

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106: CAD 100 per month per return, maximum CAD 2,500 per party; missing or incomplete T106 documentation can trigger the transfer-pricing penalty under s. 247(3) of 10% of the net upward adjustment; deficient T106 filing can extend the CRA reassessment window by 3 years under s. 152(4)
